review.authorization: Active goal and standing autonomous approval for documented native screening reconstructions.
review.basis: Useful heat, 90% capture and original 9% penalty on inspected native allocated stack; correct post-combustion chain rather than workbook oxy-fuel linkage.
limitations: Complete native German exergy-allocated coal CHP heat is the fixed screening basis in all IAM regions. Retain the original useful-heat CCS model 9% heat penalty and 90% capture of attributable allocated fossil stack CO2. Do not infer physical efficiency by inverting allocated fuel draw.

Native heat consumes 0.77 MJ of German coal combustion service per MJ heat, with 0.094634 kg fossil CO2/MJ fuel service. After 1.09 heat input the gross allocated stack is 0.0794263162 kg/MJ; capture demand and its paired negative fossil stack correction are 0.07148368458 kg/MJ. The old 0.048181815 kg credit would capture only 60.6623% of this stack.

Use the complete CLIC post-combustion coal capture, 200 km pipeline and 1000 m storage chain, correcting the old post-labelled workbook linkage to oxy-fuel capture. Capture energy, infrastructure, pipeline, storage leakage and emissions remain complete. No second capture credit, avoided heat/electricity output or extra distribution loss is added.

German CHP allocation, geographic extrapolation, historical plant fleet, capture technology and energy penalty, upstream fuel, vintage and score differences remain screening limitations. A unique fixed-reference bridge prevents regional relinking from replacing the reviewed stack allocation while retaining its fixed capture credit.

TIAM coke-with-CCS retains Premise’s existing hard-coal CHP screening convention. Coke chemistry and fuel production are not reconstructed; this is an explicit fuel/technology proxy. Full combined-fuels IAM qualification remains pending.
